newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese creditors liquidate Mineralbank's samurai.
newsitem.headline: Japanese creditors liquidate Mineralbank's samurai.

text.p: Some Japanese creditors have sold off samurai bonds issued by Bulgaria's troubled state-owned Mineralbank, which failed to redeem five billion yen worth of those bonds in mid-June, creditors said on Friday.
The samurai bonds had been bought entirely by Japanese investors through a private placement arranged by the Industrial Bank of Japan (IBJ) in 1989.
"We've sold Mineralbank's samurai bonds to a foreign account," a senior official at a creditor told Reuters.
"Naturally, under this situation we thought it was still better to liquidate, even at a big discount," he said.
An official at another creditor institution said it had sold these samurai bonds to an international fund operator through a European bank.
"I believe bigger investors have taken losses, but smaller ones could still be holding on to those bonds," he added.
Media reports say about 18 Japanese financial institutions, including life and non-life insurers, city and local banks and smaller investors, own the issues.
The fund operators are believed to have bought these bonds at a huge discount on the slim possibility that the bonds could be redeemed in the future, financial sources said.
Both officials declined to comment on when their institutions sold the samurais.
On Wednesday, an insolvency suit against the Mineralbank was postponed indefinitely after a bomb threat closed the court building.
The IBJ is talking with Bulgarian authorities about means of repayment, but the discussions have not produced results so far.

"There's no guarantee that we will get paid back even if we waited longer," the second official said. "We took a loss but we think it's better than getting nothing." -- Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
